## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 7.729 at N=4000 (past the L1d spill at N≈963) to 5.128 at N=65000 (just past the L2 spill at N≈61680), then continues declining slightly to 4.897 at N=4000000. There is no knee at the L2→DRAM spill; the curve is pure overhead amortization at small N flattening to a DRAM-streaming floor. Death rate raises this floor without reshaping the N-curve: at q=0.25 the floor is ~7.93 ns/p, at q=0.1 ~6.17, at q=0.05 ~5.70 — all monotonically declining with N in the same pattern. At q=0.5 the curve goes nearly flat at ~27.3 ns/p across all N, indicating a regime change where branchy-respawn cost dominates over memory cost.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 13.89 GB/s at N=4000000, q=0.01 — 55% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is bandwidth-bound at low churn but never approaches the ceiling. Bandwidth falls with death rate: 13.89→11.93→11.02→8.57 GB/s for q=0.01→0.05→0.1→0.25, then collapses to 2.49 GB/s at q=0.5. The transition from bandwidth-bound to overhead-bound occurs between q=0.25 and q=0.5, where the branchy respawn path (`udiv`, `bl spawn`, RNG refill) dominates.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` process four float components of a single 68-byte particle together, with `ext.16b` rearranging lanes and `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` performing an indexed single-element load — a gather — for one component. The render phase uses `uqadd.8b` for 8-way byte saturating adds but writes pixels via 19 `strb` byte stores. These byte-granular scatters, plus the scalar `udiv`/`bl` respawn path, explain why bandwidth caps at 55% of ceiling rather than approaching it.

## Verdict
Partially — at q=0.01 the algo sustains 13.89 GB/s = 55% of ceiling with no cache-spill knee, confirming the N-curve shape the hypothesis predicts, but 55% is not "approaching" the ceiling. Component-wise auto-vectorization (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) is present, yet the byte-scatter stores (`strb`) and branchy respawn (`udiv`, `bl spawn`) cap bandwidth, and at q=0.5 it collapses to 2.49 GB/s = 10% of ceiling. The hypothesis holds only in the low-churn regime and only partially even there.
